sources.name: Maternal-Newborn Nursing: Barrier Methods of Contraception
sources.text: 5.3 Barrier Methods of Contraception Learning Objectives By the end of this section, you will be able to: Compare and contrast the risks, benefits, advantages, and disadvantages of barrier contraception methods Discuss population-focused use of barrier contraception methods Preventing pregnancy using a barrier method blocks the passage of sperm through the reproductive tract, which prevents the sperm from reaching the egg for fertilization. Barrier methods of contraception are useful for those who cannot use hormonal contraception due to current or previous medical history or those not wanting hormonal birth control. Barrier methods offer a cost-effective and safe way to prevent pregnancy without having to meet with a health-care provider. sources.name: Fundamentals of Nursing: Barriers to Communication
sources.text: Physical Barriers A physical barrier is one of the biggest challenges to communication. Physical barriers include noise, architecture, environment , time, or distance ( Table 2.7 ). Nurses can use written communication if they are unable to decrease the noise to overcome the communication barrier. Other stimuli, such as cell phones and televisions, also can prevent messages from being received. Nurses may not be able to check all orders immediately; however, the nurse should recognize the timeliness of their response can overcome the communication barrier. The nurse interrupts the patient to explain they have to return and will be right back, but the nurse does not return for two hours. Sometimes technology can overcome a distance barrier, but that implies that the patient has access to technology.
